assertions.name: h_frame_swing_equals_u_frame_swing
assertions.source: Matched magnification, so the comparison is fair. The two frames swing identically — changing the expansion variable does not change the anchor-instability at all.

assertions.name: both_swings_equal_the_residual_swing
assertions.source: u-frame 0.023747804, h-frame 0.023748163, residual 0.023747189. The coefficient swing IS the residual swing; the divisors contribute ~1e-6. So the instability is a property of the model's q-dependence, not of the coordinate.

description: Tests whether re-expressing the Q_β ladder in h = q − 1/q instead of u = b·ℏ_q² fixes the cross-anchor instability of the extracted coefficients. Extracts the same residual in both frames at MATCHED magnification (h^k chosen so h^k ≈ u³) so neither frame is flattered by a smaller divisor. Result: both swing identically to five significant figures, and both equal the swing of the residual itself — the instability is in the residual, not the coordinate. Refutes the leakage hypothesis as the explanation of this drift (scope-(a)). The h-reframe keeps its other justifications (analyticity, odd-rung expressiveness, Ohtsuki/Habiro alignment, α_EM consistency) but buys nothing numerical at ~3× the rungs. No fit; nothing wired.
